3FIUVX3ffG.claimed_gains: Synthesis outperforms search on reasoning-intensive fine-tuning (75.46% vs. 34.52%) while trailing slightly on knowledge-intensive fine-tuning (43.67% vs. 45.29%), and Retrieve-Transform-Synthesize reaches 32.4% normalized fine-tune performance on DatasetResearch-Pro versus 24.1% for the strongest pure workflow and 52.3% for humans.

1UUiXNNCyo.one_liner: Outcome-backed action contrasts select decision states where log-probability differences under privileged action guidance augment token-level advantages.
1UUiXNNCyo.problem: Terminal rewards give sparse decision feedback for long-horizon LLM agents, while unselective privileged distillation fails to identify where guidance is needed and conflates action preferences with added context.
1UUiXNNCyo.method: Contrastive Privileged Action Distillation (CPAD) matches repeated decision states across on-policy rollouts and selects states where downstream outcomes favor a preferred action over an inferior alternative. At selected states, the model re-scores its response under contexts differing only in the guiding action and uses the token-level log-probability difference to augment outcome advantages during training.
1UUiXNNCyo.key_idea: Select repeated rollout states with outcome-supported action preferences and augment token-level advantages using log-probability differences between preferred and inferior privileged action contexts.
1UUiXNNCyo.evidence: Evaluated on ALFWorld seen tasks and WebShop using Qwen2.5 models at 1.5B, 3B, and 7B against HGPO, GiGPO, GraphGPO, and matched GRPO.
1UUiXNNCyo.claimed_gains: CPAD exceeds HGPO, GiGPO, and GraphGPO in success AUC within common training-time budgets across all six settings and improves final success and validation AUC over matched GRPO.

y89ckFndSX.one_liner: Canonical runtime event traces and sequence-normalized policy optimization train generative safety guards across heterogeneous computer-use agents.
y89ckFndSX.problem: Static prompt-response guards miss runtime execution hazards of computer-use agents, while token-level post-training lets longer rationales dominate generative guard updates.
y89ckFndSX.method: HazardAuditor executes heterogeneous agents in controlled environments and normalizes their browser, terminal, filesystem, and service interactions into a canonical event representation. Guard Policy Optimization (GuardPO) converts deterministic safety outcomes into sequence-level advantages and normalizes rationale and verdict regions.
y89ckFndSX.key_idea: Normalize heterogeneous agent runtime interactions into canonical events and optimize generative guards with sequence-level advantages normalized separately across rationale and verdict spans.
y89ckFndSX.evidence: Evaluated across multiple benchmarks and heterogeneous computer-use agent frameworks including Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, and OpenClaw.
y89ckFndSX.claimed_gains: HazardAuditor improves accuracy by up to 16.5 percentage points over the strongest prior guard across evaluated benchmarks and computer-use systems.

xeqhKFXC9z.one_liner: Voxel-level spatial-semantic compression and recoverable layer-skipping group routing reduce multi-view visual computation in 3D VLMs.
xeqhKFXC9z.problem: Multi-view 3D vision-language models incur high inference cost from cross-view redundant tokens and from processing all visual tokens across every LLM layer.
xeqhKFXC9z.method: GeoGR applies projector-level GeoSemZip to consolidate multi-view observations into 3D voxel tokens selected by semantic saliency and spatial coverage while aggregating unselected voxels into contextual anchors. Inside the LLM, GroupRoute combines late entry, early exit, and recoverable group-wise layer skipping so low-relevance tokens bypass layers and rejoin at budgeted anchor layers.
xeqhKFXC9z.key_idea: Compress multi-view inputs into saliency-and-coverage 3D voxel tokens with contextual anchors, then route low-relevance tokens around LLM layers with recoverable re-entry.
xeqhKFXC9z.evidence: Includes compression-aware post-training on a 67K-sample dataset retaining 30% of the original data; evaluation details are truncated in the abstract.

yMfo5ZPJkw.one_liner: In-context relational world model predicts sparse structured database edits induced by actions from observed execution histories.
yMfo5ZPJkw.problem: Standard relational learning predicts from static database states rather than inferring how unseen system-specific dynamics mutate database records under actions.
yMfo5ZPJkw.method: WorldRel procedurally generates executable relational worlds for pretraining TabWM, a tabular world model. Given a few observed action-execution traces from an unseen database system as context, TabWM predicts the sparse structured edits (operation, relational location, and value) caused by new actions without parameter updates and rolls them forward recursively for planning.
yMfo5ZPJkw.key_idea: Condition a pretrained relational model on observed execution traces in context to predict explicit structured database edits and roll them forward recursively.
yMfo5ZPJkw.evidence: Pretrained with WorldRel and evaluated across 512 held-out executable relational worlds on edit prediction and multi-step action selection via search.
yMfo5ZPJkw.claimed_gains: Across 512 held-out worlds, complete-edit F1 increases from 0.016 with zero observed executions to 0.685 with 64 observed executions.

6WbaSK2rDP.one_liner: Complex-STFT audio autoencoder uses per-bin periodic activations and cross-channel interaction to reconstruct high-fidelity stereo music.
6WbaSK2rDP.problem: Waveform audio autoencoders lack an explicit frequency axis for per-band correction, leading to high-frequency loss, phase incoherence, and stereo-image collapse under compression.
6WbaSK2rDP.method: ear-VAE2 encodes stereo music in the complex STFT domain with direct access to per-bin magnitude and phase and cross-channel left-right interaction. It introduces Spec-SnakeBeta, which learns a periodic activation per frequency bin initialized in log-parameter space, alongside a Duplex-Aware module (truncated in the abstract).
6WbaSK2rDP.key_idea: Autoencode stereo audio over complex STFT coefficients using frequency-bin-specific periodic activations with frequency-dependent log-space initialization and cross-channel interaction.
6WbaSK2rDP.evidence: Supported by a controlled study of five matched-budget representations and controlled activation ablations (downstream evaluation truncated in the abstract).

JNAe5EpbjI.one_liner: Event-aware sparse attention and multiscale spatiotemporal vector quantization jointly localize and classify events in continuous EEG.
JNAe5EpbjI.problem: Asynchronous EEG event detection must isolate event classes and temporal onsets and offsets from continuous neural background activity without predefined boundaries.
JNAe5EpbjI.method: NeuroDETR applies FOCAL, an event-aware sparse attention module guided by predicted event presence, to refine temporal features and aggregate spatial context before tokenization. Multiscale temporal codebooks and hierarchical Spatial-Pyramid VQ then build a compact discrete event memory for joint classification and boundary estimation.
JNAe5EpbjI.key_idea: Refine continuous EEG with event-guided sparse attention, then quantize features through multiscale temporal codebooks and hierarchical spatial-pyramid vector quantization.
JNAe5EpbjI.evidence: Evaluated on eight EEG datasets spanning diverse brain-computer interface paradigms.

SsjhVTW9zo.one_liner: Benchmarks whether multimodal models distinguish visible appearances from physical entities when counting reflected or transmitted objects.
SsjhVTW9zo.problem: Visual counting benchmarks rarely separate enumerating image appearances from recovering the distinct physical entities that produced them.
SsjhVTW9zo.method: PhysCount annotates target appearances, observation modes, and shared entity identities across real-world images. Four question families test appearance counting, entity counting, image-formation-specific counting, and appearance-entity correspondence.
SsjhVTW9zo.key_idea: Link annotated appearances to physical entity identities and evaluate both counts and their correspondence across observation modes.
SsjhVTW9zo.evidence: The benchmark contains 546 real-world images, 4,595 human-written questions, and 651 target-specific groups, evaluated across 43 MLLMs using per-family and whole-group accuracy.
SsjhVTW9zo.claimed_gains: Even the strongest model answers every question correctly in only 16.28% of groups.

WxOx7Kok46.one_liner: Augments distribution-matching distillation with EMA-feature mean and standard-deviation constraints for few-step image generation.
WxOx7Kok46.problem: One- and few-step text-to-image distillation may benefit from explicit moment constraints on internally estimated score supervision.
WxOx7Kok46.method: IDM retains the full DMD correction while matching generator-EMA feature means and per-coordinate standard deviations. A reverse-KL decomposition into Gaussian moment and non-Gaussian residual terms motivates the added constraints without an external feature encoder.
WxOx7Kok46.key_idea: Constrain Gaussian feature moments using the generator’s EMA copy while preserving the complete internal distribution-matching score correction.
WxOx7Kok46.evidence: Full-parameter and LoRA experiments on Z-Image-Turbo 6B and Qwen-Image 20B include moment-loss ablations and comparisons between EMA and external DINOv2 features.
WxOx7Kok46.claimed_gains: At two network evaluations, IDM reaches 94.25% and 90.20% on Chinese and English LongText-Bench, respectively.

V0dfRkM2lE.one_liner: Learns internal real and fake flow trajectories through deterministic condition shifting for one-step text-to-image generation.
V0dfRkM2lE.problem: Distribution-matching feedback for one-step generation often requires an auxiliary generated-distribution network whose training cost grows with the backbone.
V0dfRkM2lE.method: APEX learns the real trajectory under the original condition and the generated trajectory under a deterministically shifted condition using flow matching on its own outputs. Evaluating both velocities at the same sample and time yields an internal distribution-matching correction without a separate fake-score network.
V0dfRkM2lE.key_idea: Use deterministic condition shifts to host real and generated trajectory predictions in one model and difference their velocities for score correction.
V0dfRkM2lE.evidence: Score–velocity duality supports the internal correction, but the provided abstract does not state evaluation datasets or empirical results.

7DrkJNzqyF.one_liner: Retrieves relevant historical latents to condition autoregressive video diffusion beyond its recent sliding window.
7DrkJNzqyF.problem: Sliding-window autoregressive video generation irreversibly conditions on accumulated appearance errors, causing long-horizon error accumulation and identity drift.
7DrkJNzqyF.method: LongLive-RAG treats previously generated latents as a searchable history and retrieves relevant entries with a query embedding for each new block. A Window Temporal Delta Loss suppresses redundant local similarity so embeddings capture meaningful temporal changes.
7DrkJNzqyF.key_idea: Retrieve non-local historical latents using embeddings trained to emphasize temporal changes rather than redundant within-window similarity.
7DrkJNzqyF.evidence: Experiments evaluate the framework across multiple autoregressive video backbones and generation lengths.

aCe7O7tAOd.one_liner: Subtracts a learned channel-wise highlight attenuation map before log-domain ratio formation for low-light scene understanding.
aCe7O7tAOd.problem: Local highlights introduce channel-dependent biases in log images before ratio construction, corrupting illumination-invariant features.
aCe7O7tAOd.method: HDRNet predicts a bounded, channel-wise attenuation map from RGB cues to suppress highlight bias prior to log-ratio computation, then fuses spatial and spectral ratio branches with RGB features under Highlight Prior Regularization.
aCe7O7tAOd.key_idea: Predicts a bounded channel-wise attenuation map to subtract highlight bias before log-domain color-ratio construction, then fuses dual-domain features.
aCe7O7tAOd.evidence: Evaluations on ExDark, DarkFace, LIS, and ACDC-Night, plus breakdowns by official lighting labels.
aCe7O7tAOd.claimed_gains: Delivers mAP gains of 2.2 points on ExDark and 2.6 points on DarkFace, and achieves 42.0% mask AP on LIS and 62.1% mIoU on ACDC-Night.

8Awrl0pIuq.one_liner: Probes dynamical parameters in frozen time-series foundation models and compares hidden-state accessibility against forecast response.
8Awrl0pIuq.problem: Time-series foundation models may encode dynamical properties in hidden states without faithfully expressing them in their forecasts.
8Awrl0pIuq.method: The authors formalize Dynamical Parameters (trend slope, oscillation frequency, autoregressive dependence) and measure both hidden-state recovery (accessibility) and forecast agreement with law-conditioned references. They further apply constructed hidden-state interventions to separate representation capacity from input-induced bypass pathways.
8Awrl0pIuq.key_idea: Comparing hidden-state probing against law-conditioned forecast responses and hidden-state edits separates representation accessibility from forecast expression in TSFMs.
8Awrl0pIuq.evidence: Evaluates nine frozen time-series foundation models across thirteen dynamical laws (63 model-parameter cells).
8Awrl0pIuq.claimed_gains: 42 of 63 model-parameter cells exceed 0.95 accessibility while median reference-aligned forecast response is 0.46; input changes transmit a median aligned gain of 0.34.

1Kxk30PvqF.one_liner: Discovers executable test-time scaling controllers for joint user accuracy, latency, and cost constraints via amortized agentic search in PersonTTS.
1Kxk30PvqF.problem: Existing test-time scaling methods optimize accuracy against a single resource metric rather than jointly satisfying user-specific accuracy, latency, and cost requirements.
1Kxk30PvqF.method: The authors propose PersonTTS, an amortized agentic policy-discovery framework that initializes candidate executable controllers and distills procedural guidance from prior users' search experience while evaluating every candidate on the target user profile.
1Kxk30PvqF.key_idea: Amortizing agentic controller discovery via target-evaluated initialization and source-distilled procedural guidance adapts test-time scaling to multi-dimensional user preferences.
1Kxk30PvqF.evidence: Experiments on AIME, HMMT, GPQA-Diamond, and LiveCodeBench evaluating unseen user profiles and held-out problems.

K8FwvsbZjU.one_liner: Compresses multi-vector visual document retrieval indexes by prioritizing vector coverage over numerical precision with geometry-calibrated MaxSim scoring.
K8FwvsbZjU.problem: Multi-vector indexes for visual document retrieval incur prohibitive storage costs, and aggressive compression distorts vector geometry and MaxSim scoring.
K8FwvsbZjU.method: BaMIC allocates storage budgets by prioritizing document-side vector coverage over per-vector bit precision, selects representations per budget, and applies training-free geometry-calibrated scoring to correct compression-induced radial score bias.
K8FwvsbZjU.key_idea: Prioritizes retaining document vector cardinality over per-vector precision and corrects sub-bit radial MaxSim bias via training-free geometry calibration.
K8FwvsbZjU.evidence: Evaluated across multiple visual document retrieval benchmarks under varying storage budgets.

PCAODQ61Qw.one_liner: Compresses KV caches via a closed-form low-rank key surrogate aligned to attention distributions and learned global top-k rank allocation.
PCAODQ61Qw.problem: Long-context LLM inference is memory-bound by KV-cache growth, while compressing raw keys or logits misaligns with downstream attention weights.
PCAODQ61Qw.method: BELT minimizes an attention-distribution surrogate yielding a closed-form low-rank key solution, paired with a learned global rank allocator using soft selection during training and hard top-k selection at inference, plus Triton kernels.
PCAODQ61Qw.key_idea: Targets attention distributions rather than raw keys via a closed-form quadratic surrogate and allocates ranks globally with differentiable-to-hard top-k selection.
PCAODQ61Qw.evidence: Evaluated across three LLMs on LongBench and throughput benchmarks with Triton GPU kernels and cache quantization.
PCAODQ61Qw.claimed_gains: Achieves up to 70% low-rank KV cache compression while outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 23.3 points on LongBench, up to 17.8x overall reduction with quantization, 2.7x attention speedup, and 3.3x end-to-end decoding throughput.

MpNPoDTf3B.one_liner: Migrates frozen downstream consumers to upgraded representation autoencoders using consumer-supervised functional maps.
MpNPoDTf3B.problem: Upgrading representation autoencoders changes coordinate semantics even when tensor shapes match, breaking frozen downstream consumers.
MpNPoDTf3B.method: Consumer-Typed Functional Migration (CTFM) learns a release-wide repair map around a calibrated base supervised by archived consumer responses. It offers IQ-SAFE (preserving pooled coordinates) and QUALITY (full-field correction) modes, compiled into a low-rank or full affine map on RAEv2.
MpNPoDTf3B.key_idea: Supervises a release-wide functional repair map with archived consumer responses while optionally preserving base-calibrated pooled coordinates.
MpNPoDTf3B.evidence: Evaluations across DINO-based RAEv2, Perception Encoder RAEs, and 3,232 new RAEv2 fields measuring recognition, fidelity, and distribution quality.

JJjf2Sj6zX.one_liner: Pairs local point-pair subset sampling with an invertible structure-nuisance factorization for single-scan self-supervised point cloud denoising.
JJjf2Sj6zX.problem: Splitting a single noisy point cloud scan into two subsets for Noise2Noise training introduces a coupling gap because subsets sample different surface locations with different local densities.
JJjf2Sj6zX.method: A coupled paired-subset sampler constructs subsets from local point pairs to bound the coupling gap. An invertible network then factorizes latents into a subset-invariant structure stream and a subset-specific nuisance stream, training with Earth Mover's Distance, entropic optimal-transport latent consistency, and displacement regularization without clean targets.
JJjf2Sj6zX.key_idea: Bounds single-scan subset discrepancy via local point-pair sampling and factorizes latents invertibly into subset-invariant structure and subset-specific nuisance streams.
JJjf2Sj6zX.evidence: Experiments on single-scan point cloud denoising are mentioned in the abstract, though specific datasets and baselines are not detailed.

nOpUIp4pqm.one_liner: Routes each voxel softly among fixed-coordinate history, velocity-addressed history, and current evidence for roadside occupancy.
nOpUIp4pqm.problem: Temporal memory in fixed roadside cameras improves weak observations but corrupts occupancy predictions when moving traffic leaves stale history.
nOpUIp4pqm.method: RoadOcc uses dynamic-aware cross-attention, multi-scale voxel velocity estimation (VVE), and velocity-guided dynamic sparse fusion (VDSF) to softly route voxels among Persist, Transport, and Refresh sources.
nOpUIp4pqm.key_idea: Learns supervised soft routing per voxel across fixed-coordinate history, velocity-transported history, and current observations.
nOpUIp4pqm.evidence: Evaluations on InfraOcc, Occ3D-nuScenes, two transfer models, longer intervals, and three-seed ablations.
nOpUIp4pqm.claimed_gains: On InfraOcc, RoadOcc reaches 65.29 mIoU and 32.37 dynamic mIoU, gains of 4.44 and 4.71 over STCOcc; VVE raises dynamic mIoU by 0.87 and supervised P/T/R adds 1.40 dynamic points.

vsiVsJWvnz.one_liner: Self-distills trait-conditioned LLM safety behavior toward no-trait behavior within an identified low-dimensional trait subspace.
vsiVsJWvnz.problem: System-prompt traits cause LLMs to make inconsistent refusal and compliance decisions on identical user requests.
vsiVsJWvnz.method: The paper introduces Trait-Induced Deviation and Flip Rate metrics, identifies a low-dimensional trait perturbation subspace, and proposes TraSN to self-distill trait-conditioned outputs to no-trait behavior only inside that subspace.
vsiVsJWvnz.key_idea: Neutralizes trait-induced safety shifts by self-distilling trait-conditioned representations toward the no-trait baseline strictly within a low-dimensional trait subspace.
vsiVsJWvnz.evidence: Representation-level analysis and experiments evaluating trait-invariant safety, harmful-request refusal, and general capability preservation.

fx6TAsHANs.one_liner: Performs mask-free, end-to-end audio-visual person swapping, insertion, and deletion using a 100K dual-reference dataset.
fx6TAsHANs.problem: Separate video and audio editing pipelines with spatial masks suffer from poor lip-audio synchronization, cumulative errors, and mask-size trade-offs.
fx6TAsHANs.method: AVE unifies reference-guided person swap, insert, and delete across audio and video without spatial masks, trained on a 100K dual-reference AVE-Dataset using Synthetic-to-Real reconstruction and audio warm-up.
fx6TAsHANs.key_idea: Unifies mask-free audio-visual human editing in a single end-to-end model trained with Synthetic-to-Real reconstruction and preliminary audio warm-up.
fx6TAsHANs.evidence: Evaluations comparing AVE against modality-separate audio-visual editing pipelines on realism, temporal consistency, and lip-audio alignment.

1ds3a38Ku9.one_liner: Aligns intermediate MLLM visual tokens with 3D geometry features via learned SE(3)-equivariant pose transformations without inference-time 3D encoders.
1ds3a38Ku9.problem: Input-level fusion of 3D geometry encoders into MLLMs fails to supervise intermediate layers, causing geometric alignment to weaken in deeper layers.
1ds3a38Ku9.method: Geo-REPA introduces learned pose tokens that predict per-frame rotations and translations to apply SE(3) transformations to visual feature triplets, supervising both transformed visual tokens and pose tokens against a 3D geometry encoder during training only.
1ds3a38Ku9.key_idea: Predicts per-frame SE(3) transformations via learned pose tokens to align intermediate MLLM visual features with 3D geometry representations during training.
1ds3a38Ku9.evidence: Evaluations and ablations on VSI-Bench, SQA3D, and Scan2Cap across MLLM backbones.

REE0TB9Fde.one_liner: Coordinates a VLM, video generation model, and action expert for robot manipulation through shared learnable Predictive Intent tokens.
REE0TB9Fde.problem: Directly fusing VLMs and video generation models via shared multi-layer attention can interfere with their specialized semantic and world-modeling capabilities.
REE0TB9Fde.method: PINT inserts learnable Intent Tokens into the VLM sequence to condition both a video generation model and an action expert, training in two stages so future video prediction shapes Predictive Intent before adapting the video and action experts.
REE0TB9Fde.key_idea: Conditions a video world model and action expert on shared VLM Intent Tokens trained across native prediction objectives in two stages.
REE0TB9Fde.evidence: In-distribution and out-of-distribution robot manipulation evaluations without embodied pretraining.

zYUaM9Xm0l.one_liner: Corrects RLVR policy gradients for asymmetric false-positive and false-negative verifier noise using backward and forward reward hooks.
zYUaM9Xm0l.problem: Binary automated verifiers in RL with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) introduce asymmetric false-positive and false-negative noise that biases policy-gradient updates.
zYUaM9Xm0l.method: Formalizing verifier errors as an asymmetric stochastic channel, the authors derive a backward surrogate-reward correction for unbiased gradients and a forward score-function reweighting using only the false-negative rate, estimated online via an appeals mechanism inside GRPO.
zYUaM9Xm0l.key_idea: Models imperfect verifiers as an asymmetric binary noise channel to derive backward unbiased reward corrections and forward score-function reweighting with online FN-rate estimation.
zYUaM9Xm0l.evidence: Implemented in a GRPO pipeline and evaluated on reasoning tasks under both synthetic and real verifier noise.

j0zCGq1kOr.one_liner: Updates an automated jailbreak attacker's weights via policy gradients per target behavior during test time.
j0zCGq1kOr.problem: Existing automated red-teaming attackers keep weights frozen during an attack on a target behavior, discarding gathered victim feedback after the context window ends.
j0zCGq1kOr.method: Red-TTT performs per-behavior test-time training: at each round, the attacker samples candidate prompts, scores them against victim replies using a composite reward adapted for best-sample success, and takes a policy-gradient update before the next round.
j0zCGq1kOr.key_idea: Consolidates victim feedback into attacker weights mid-attack via per-behavior policy-gradient updates optimized for single-best-sample jailbreak success.
j0zCGq1kOr.evidence: Evaluated with budget-matched extra-sampling controls using only sampling access to victim models.

XS1t7JP5FD.one_liner: Restores generative diversity in visual autoregressive models without training by suppressing a pivotal feature component at input and amplifying it at output.
XS1t7JP5FD.problem: Visual Autoregressive (VAR) next-scale prediction models suffer from diversity collapse, reducing output variability across samples.
XS1t7JP5FD.method: DiverseVAR identifies a pivotal feature-map component governing early-scale diversity formation. During training-free inference, it suppresses this pivotal component in the model input and amplifies it in the model output to recover diversity while preserving image fidelity.
XS1t7JP5FD.key_idea: Suppresses a diversity-governing pivotal feature-map component in VAR inputs and amplifies it in outputs during inference without retraining.
XS1t7JP5FD.evidence: Empirically evaluated on VAR text-to-image synthesis for generative diversity and fidelity.

QIfegZcORG.one_liner: Formulates robust Gaussian covariance estimation under epsilon-contamination as a nonconvex objective solvable by first-order methods.
QIfegZcORG.problem: Estimating high-dimensional Gaussian covariance when an epsilon-fraction of samples are arbitrarily corrupted is challenging for standard first-order optimization.
QIfegZcORG.method: The authors propose a nonconvex 1D variance objective whose approximate first-order stationary points are provably near-optimal, then extend it to high dimensions via a tractable relaxation and heuristic first-order algorithm.
QIfegZcORG.key_idea: Constructs a nonconvex objective whose approximate first-order stationary points yield near-optimal variance estimates under arbitrary sample corruption.
QIfegZcORG.evidence: Theoretical stationary-point optimality analysis in 1D and empirical comparisons against existing robust covariance estimators in high dimensions.
QIfegZcORG.claimed_gains: Achieves empirical performance comparable to existing robust covariance estimation algorithms (exact numbers not stated in abstract).

wBNqzHsvaM.one_liner: Studies how on-policy distillation task vectors compose with RL teacher updates and across different tasks.
wBNqzHsvaM.problem: The composability of task vectors produced by on-policy distillation (OPD) relative to reinforcement learning (RL) teacher updates remains largely unexplored.
wBNqzHsvaM.method: The authors evaluate merging OPD task vectors with RL teacher task vectors within a task and composing OPD task vectors across tasks, alongside parameter-space analyses of update collinearity and top-10% feed-forward channel overlap.
wBNqzHsvaM.key_idea: Compares within-task and cross-task merging of on-policy distillation task vectors against RL task vectors via parameter-space collinearity and channel-overlap analyses.
wBNqzHsvaM.evidence: Evaluated across five domains, two model architectures, eight backbone-merging-rule comparisons, and a CODE-domain experiment on SmolLM3-3B.
wBNqzHsvaM.claimed_gains: OPD task-vector compositions achieve higher average scores than RL compositions in 7 of 8 backbone-merging-rule comparisons.

SiF9YBf3x7.one_liner: Adapts frozen generative speech enhancers to acoustic shifts by profiling and selecting inference hyperparameters on paired target data.
SiF9YBf3x7.problem: Fixed inference strategies for diffusion and flow-matching speech enhancers do not consistently preserve their advantage under acoustic distribution shifts.
SiF9YBf3x7.method: Situated Inference evaluates a structured inference space—varying observation processing, reverse starting point, and solver step count—on paired target speech to build a quality-computation profile. It then selects and fixes one strategy to maximize quality or minimize compute subject to default quality.
SiF9YBf3x7.key_idea: Profiles observation processing, reverse start point, and solver steps on paired target speech to select a fixed inference configuration for a frozen enhancer.
SiF9YBf3x7.evidence: Evaluated across four generative speech enhancement backbones, three acoustic conditions, and deployment on an Ameca humanoid robot.

jJbc2wpXoo.one_liner: Approximates large-batch online entropic optimal transport couplings to reduce gradient variance and integration error in flow matching.
jJbc2wpXoo.problem: Small-batch optimal transport couplings limit variance reduction in flow matching, while exact large-minibatch OT at every step is computationally prohibitive.
jJbc2wpXoo.method: The paper develops a scalable online entropic OT approximation for pairing source and target samples in large minibatches and proves strict reductions in full stochastic-gradient variance and integration error as coupling size grows.
jJbc2wpXoo.key_idea: Scales flow-matching source-target pairing via an online entropic optimal transport approximation across large minibatches.
jJbc2wpXoo.evidence: Supported by theoretical variance/integration-error bounds and experiments on single-cell and image-flow training.

uTIoY3tprZ.one_liner: Introduces Monotonic Uncertainty Regularization to prevent per-sample predictive uncertainty from rising as richer information is acquired.
uTIoY3tprZ.problem: Although average uncertainty falls as inputs gain signal, uncertainty increases for 49.8--90.4% of individual samples during progressive information acquisition.
uTIoY3tprZ.method: The paper diagnoses this aggregate monotonicity illusion and proposes Monotonic Uncertainty Regularization (MUR), a family of lightweight fine-tuning objectives that couple predictions for the same sample across progressive information levels.
uTIoY3tprZ.key_idea: Regularizes fine-tuning by linking a sample's predictions across successive information levels so per-sample uncertainty decreases monotonically.
uTIoY3tprZ.evidence: Evaluated across Imagenette, ImageNet-1k, and chest X-ray classification over multiple architectures, alongside a blinded radiologist comparison.
uTIoY3tprZ.claimed_gains: Without regularization, individual-sample uncertainty increases with added signal for 49.8--90.4% of samples across the three datasets.

PTL1u5Zn05.one_liner: Extracts a task-aware Hessian proxy from fine-tuning weight deltas to guide calibration-free low-bit quantization.
PTL1u5Zn05.problem: Calibration-free post-training quantization suffers sharp accuracy drops at low bit-widths because it ignores task-specific weight sensitivity.
PTL1u5Zn05.method: TIGER-Q derives a task-aware subspace basis from the task vector (fine-tuned minus pre-trained weights) as a data-free Hessian proxy, then alternates closed-form continuous scale updates with local discrete weight search and row-wise monotonic acceptance.
PTL1u5Zn05.key_idea: Uses the task vector between fine-tuned and pre-trained weights as a data-free Hessian proxy for decoupled scale-and-weight quantization.
PTL1u5Zn05.evidence: Evaluated on both language and vision models against calibration-free quantization baselines.

sGVZRmZQzK.one_liner: Steals an adapted tabular foundation model via random queries and uses the surrogate to amplify membership, attribute, and property inference attacks.
sGVZRmZQzK.problem: Adapted tabular foundation models (TFMs) may leak private in-context training examples even to adversaries with only query access and no in-distribution data.
sGVZRmZQzK.method: An adversary sends random queries to a deployed TFM, adapts a public TFM checkpoint to the returned predictions to build a high-fidelity surrogate, and runs membership, attribute, and property inference attacks against the surrogate.
sGVZRmZQzK.key_idea: Trains a surrogate TFM on random-query outputs of a deployed model to enable unrestricted white-box privacy attacks on private in-context data.
sGVZRmZQzK.evidence: Analyzed across multiple datasets, TFM backbones, context sizes, and output formats (probabilities vs. predicted labels).

9FaUYSuhHT.one_liner: Decouples geometrically supervised scene understanding and affordance prediction with closed-loop recovery for robotic manipulation in smoke.
9FaUYSuhHT.problem: Dynamic, non-uniform smoke degrades RGB images and breaks active depth sensors, causing severe failures in robotic manipulation systems.
9FaUYSuhHT.method: SmokeManip decouples depth-free perception into a scene-understanding model and a conditioned object-centric affordance predictor trained with geometric supervision, paired with action primitives, closed-loop recovery, and the SmokeLab simulation platform.
9FaUYSuhHT.key_idea: Combines depth-free geometrically supervised scene-and-affordance decoupling with closed-loop primitive recovery inside a dedicated smoke simulation platform.
9FaUYSuhHT.evidence: Evaluated in the SmokeLab simulation platform for smoke-scene manipulation.

3cCUAYrxFe.one_liner: Benchmarks full-duplex speech models on when to answer, stay silent, or stop speaking in continuous 3-to-4-speaker conversations.
3cCUAYrxFe.problem: Existing full-duplex speech benchmarks test single-user turn-taking rather than multi-party conversations where assistants must track addressees continuously.
3cCUAYrxFe.method: Duplex-MPE provides 2,000 continuous audio scenarios with three or four human speakers and one assistant paired across explicit and implicit addressing, scoring initiation, accuracy, silence preservation, and stopping across eight open-weight speech models.
3cCUAYrxFe.key_idea: Evaluates continuous full-duplex speech assistants on paired explicit/implicit multi-party addressing across initiation, accuracy, silence, and stopping.
3cCUAYrxFe.evidence: Evaluated eight open-weight speech systems (including MiniCPM-o 4.5, Moshi, and FLM-Audio) and a transcript-based Gemini 3.1 Pro reference on 2,000 scenarios.
3cCUAYrxFe.claimed_gains: A transcript-based Gemini 3.1 Pro reference responds 64.3 percentage points more often to explicit than implicit requests, whereas paired tests show no significant difference for the speech systems.

zoKRDAQpft.one_liner: Learning per-sample embedding-set sizes with utility policy optimization allocates multimodal retrieval capacity according to content.
zoKRDAQpft.problem: Fixed-capacity multi-vector retrieval assigns every sample the same number of embeddings despite differences in content and retrieval difficulty.
zoKRDAQpft.method: AdaptiveEmbed introduces content-adaptive embedding sets under the SAMVR setting. Multi-Group Contrastive Learning and symmetric set-to-set similarity train structured representations, while Utility Policy Optimization chooses each sample's representation capacity.
zoKRDAQpft.key_idea: UPO allocates additional embedding vectors according to their sample-specific retrieval utility instead of fixing representation capacity globally.
zoKRDAQpft.evidence: The supplied abstract describes MGCL, SetSim, and UPO but does not state experimental settings or results.

aIio1AlTq2.one_liner: Injecting question-guided latent noise into low-relevance image tokens suppresses visual distractors without changing the MLLM backbone.
aIio1AlTq2.problem: Dense redundant image tokens dilute question-relevant visual cues and impair fine-grained reasoning in multimodal large language models.
aIio1AlTq2.method: Lens uses a temporary Lens Evidence Token to score visual-token relevance for the current question. A lightweight noise generator adds adaptive latent noise to low-relevance tokens while preserving the backbone and token sequence.
aIio1AlTq2.key_idea: Question-conditioned evidence scores guide soft latent-noise masking of irrelevant visual tokens during decoding rather than extending the reasoning trace.
aIio1AlTq2.evidence: Evaluation covers multiple VQA datasets and grounding tasks using the base MLLM with one temporary control token and a lightweight noise generator.
aIio1AlTq2.claimed_gains: Lens improves the base MLLM by 2.4-6.4 points on most VQA datasets and by 4.1-6.4 points on grounding tasks.

LH2gdpfVWQ.one_liner: Reorganizing recurrent scans, membrane-prefix reconstruction, and device-state replay accelerates direct multi-step SNN training on GPUs.
LH2gdpfVWQ.problem: Recurrent backward computation, backward-required membrane states, and persistent minibatch updates keep direct SNN training costly even after temporal fusion.
LH2gdpfVWQ.method: SpikingPhoenix changes nested recurrent and minibatch execution boundaries without changing the reference training update. SEQUENCE specializes forward-adjoint scans, SEGMENT-K reconstructs membrane prefixes during backward, and GRAPH-V2 replays compatible device-side state transitions.
LH2gdpfVWQ.key_idea: Semantics-preserving execution reordering pairs specialized recurrent scans with backward-local rematerialization and reusable device-state transitions.
LH2gdpfVWQ.evidence: Experiments include four complete CIFAR-10 schedules, graph-free ImageNet-1K recurrent workloads at T=2,4,8, mechanism-matched ablations, and update-state fidelity traces.
LH2gdpfVWQ.claimed_gains: SpikingPhoenix achieves 1.41-2.73× end-to-end speedups on CIFAR-10, and SEQUENCE achieves 1.37-1.45× geometric-mean speedups on ImageNet-1K recurrent workloads.

y01WnZj2L0.one_liner: Separates textual and visual risk routing to apply text-risk amplification and bounded refusal steering in Video LVLMs.
y01WnZj2L0.problem: Increasing video frame counts in Large Vision-Language Models improves understanding but erodes safety alignment on both explicit and video-grounded harmful requests.
y01WnZj2L0.method: The authors identify two safety-erosion mechanisms: narrowed late-layer text-risk separation for explicit harm and activation shifts along an unsafe-response direction for video-grounded harm. Their training-free defense, Risk-to-Refusal (R2R), routes requests via separate text and visual risk signals to apply text-risk amplification plus refusal steering for explicit harm and bounded refusal steering alone for grounded harm.
y01WnZj2L0.key_idea: Routes requests with separate text and visual risk detectors to selectively apply text-risk amplification and frame-bounded refusal steering.
y01WnZj2L0.evidence: Evaluated across five Large Vision-Language Models on explicit and implicit video-text harmful requests alongside representation analysis.
y01WnZj2L0.claimed_gains: Lowers attack success rates across five LVLMs to 1.5-6.9% on explicit and 2.3-8.7% on implicit harmful requests.

XvHr3TypV1.one_liner: Uses visual-geometric prototypes and an append-only output identity bank for exemplar-free cross-category incremental keypoint detection.
XvHr3TypV1.problem: Continually adding object categories with heterogeneous keypoint schemas causes either unbounded output growth or Output-Identity Collision when incompatible keypoints share head indices.
XvHr3TypV1.method: POISE (prototype-guided Persistent Output Identity Space Expansion) constructs visual-geometric prototypes and maintains an append-only output identity bank under exemplar-free top-down incremental learning. For each new category, it selectively reuses compatible identities, transfers related output parameters for initialization, and expands the bank for unmatched keypoints.
XvHr3TypV1.key_idea: Matches new category keypoints against visual-geometric prototypes to selectively reuse compatible slots or append new identities in a persistent output bank.
XvHr3TypV1.evidence: Evaluated on exemplar-free Cross-Category Incremental Keypoint Detection under the top-down setting.

aETfL2eyX3.one_liner: Augments multimodal RLVR with reference-solution reward verification and mistake-report-guided resampling on all-negative rollout groups.
aETfL2eyX3.problem: Final-answer verification in multimodal RLVR rewards flawed reasoning while hard queries produce all-negative rollout groups with no positive training signal.
aETfL2eyX3.method: ContextRL combines context-augmented reward modeling—which uses full reference solutions to verify visual grounding and reasoning and produce mistake reports—with context-augmented sampling that feeds those mistake reports to guide retry rollouts on all-negative groups.
aETfL2eyX3.key_idea: Uses full reference solutions to audit reasoning steps and generate mistake reports that guide resampling of all-negative rollout groups.
aETfL2eyX3.evidence: Trained Qwen3-VL-8B and evaluated across 11 perception and reasoning benchmarks against GRPO, DAPO, and Qwen3-VL-32B.
aETfL2eyX3.claimed_gains: Achieves average gains of 2.58% over GRPO and 1.09% over DAPO across 11 benchmarks on Qwen3-VL-8B, surpassing Qwen3-VL-32B in perception.

8afp5PuOg2.one_liner: Jointly predicts RGB, depth, geometric motion fields, and robot actions to verify candidate actions before execution.
8afp5PuOg2.problem: RGB-only world-action models must infer 3D geometry and motion from appearance alone, making them brittle under visual and domain shifts.
8afp5PuOg2.method: S4NDBOX is a 4D world-action model that jointly predicts future RGB frames, depth, view-specific geometric motion fields, and robot actions. Before execution, it uses the predicted 4D future to perform candidate action search scored by geometric agreement between imagined futures and paired actions.
8afp5PuOg2.key_idea: Predicts coupled RGB, depth, and geometric motion fields alongside actions, selecting actions via pre-execution geometric agreement verification.
8afp5PuOg2.evidence: Evaluated on RoboTwin domain-randomized tasks after clean-only training and zero-shot sim-to-real Stack Cups under pose, lighting, clutter, and camera-pose shifts.
8afp5PuOg2.claimed_gains: Improves RoboTwin hard-setting success by 13.3 percentage points over RGB-only, and raises zero-shot sim-to-real Stack Cups mean task score by 41.7 (three-view) and 40.0 (single-view) points.

MDEXA4hY7N.one_liner: Converts frozen VLM frame-relevance scores into a temporal demand distribution solved by dynamic-programming optimal transport.
MDEXA4hY7N.problem: Selecting a fixed frame budget for long-video understanding typically relies on external scorers and struggles to balance query relevance against temporal coverage.
MDEXA4hY7N.method: SAVE uses the same frozen VLM for both frame-level evidence scoring and final QA, converting relevance scores into a 1D semantic demand distribution over time. It formulates frame selection as minimizing demand-weighted squared temporal distance to the nearest selected frame and solves this optimal transport problem exactly via dynamic programming.
MDEXA4hY7N.key_idea: Solves 1D optimal transport over frozen-VLM evidential demand via exact dynamic programming to jointly optimize frame relevance and temporal coverage.
MDEXA4hY7N.evidence: Evaluated across multiple long-video benchmarks and diverse VLM architectures.

L8HbXyZbIC.one_liner: Regularizes dual-branch controllable generation by decoding side-network features to match an approximated likelihood score target.
L8HbXyZbIC.problem: The role and training efficiency of the conditional side network in frozen-backbone dual-branch controllable generation remain poorly understood and under-regularized.
L8HbXyZbIC.method: Framing the frozen main network as providing the unconditional prior score and the side branch as contributing a likelihood score, LISA hooks intermediate side-network features and projects them into score latent space via a lightweight decoder. It jointly optimizes standard diffusion loss with a distance regularization loss against an approximated likelihood score target.
L8HbXyZbIC.key_idea: Projects hooked side-branch intermediate features through a lightweight decoder to align with an approximated conditional likelihood score target.
L8HbXyZbIC.evidence: Evaluated across image and video controllable generation tasks, multiple architectures, and diffusion and flow frameworks.

nSsaEp75xm.one_liner: Embeds client-traceable black-box backdoor watermarks in federated language models via server-side token-embedding replacement without per-client retraining.
nSsaEp75xm.problem: Existing federated watermarking methods require white-box access or client cooperation, provide only group-level ownership proof, and target image classification rather than language models.
nSsaEp75xm.method: EmbTracker is a server-side watermarking framework for federated language models that embeds an API-verifiable backdoor watermark. It assigns each client a distinct registered trigger through token-embedding replacement, enabling client-level leak attribution without retraining a separate watermarked model per client.
nSsaEp75xm.key_idea: Assigns each federated learning client a unique black-box backdoor trigger via server-side token-embedding replacement to enable traceable attribution without per-client retraining.
nSsaEp75xm.evidence: Evaluated on language and vision-language models across classification, QA, and VQA under fine-tuning, pruning, quantization, noise, and watermark-overwriting attacks.
nSsaEp75xm.claimed_gains: Achieves verification rates near 100% in most settings with primary-task changes typically within 1–2 percentage points.

yFzdWNvfkV.one_liner: Shares procedural agent experiences across users while grounding execution in each receiving user's own preference memory via two-stage consolidation.
yFzdWNvfkV.problem: Isolating LLM agent memories per user prevents reusing procedural experience across users, while naively pooling memories leaks conflicting personal preferences.
yFzdWNvfkV.method: ShareMem separates shared procedural experiences—which specify how to act and which preference slots to consult—from user-local memory supplying concrete preference values. Two-stage consolidation refines experiences locally before admitting edits into the shared pool, and scope-first retrieval jointly selects local and shared entries under a fixed budget alongside a user-bound preference channel.
yFzdWNvfkV.key_idea: Decouples shared procedural experiences from user-bound preference values using two-stage consolidation and budget-bounded scope-first retrieval.
yFzdWNvfkV.evidence: Evaluated with four backbone models across Mind2Web (web navigation), VitaBench 2.0 (personalized interaction), and MemoryCode (multi-session coding) with consolidation ablations.

LJ3tnmkITu.one_liner: Partitions frozen time-series foundation model embeddings into local charts and learns gated residual transports for domain-incremental adaptation.
LJ3tnmkITu.problem: Global adaptation of pretrained time-series foundation models to new operating conditions shifts already well-classified embedding regions, causing forgetting under small calibration sets and unknown test conditions.
LJ3tnmkITu.method: PACT partitions the frozen TSFM source embedding space into local charts and learns lightweight residual transport maps only for regions affected by each arriving condition, while keeping the encoder, classifier head, and prior transports frozen. An explicit identity path is retained and a learned gate softly selects among the identity and accumulated transports without test-time condition IDs.
LJ3tnmkITu.key_idea: Learns lightweight gated residual transports on local charts of a frozen TSFM embedding space with an explicit identity path for condition-free domain-incremental adaptation.
LJ3tnmkITu.evidence: Evaluated on domain-incremental time-series classification under operating-condition drift using 5% labeled calibration data per condition and no condition identity at test time.
LJ3tnmkITu.claimed_gains: Maintains above 0.95 average macro-F1 with only 5% labeled calibration data per arriving condition and no test-time condition identity.

gCcNGnGTLX.one_liner: Detects semantic anomalies in text-attributed graphs by comparing attribute and structure community distributions and training on cross-community attribute swaps.
gCcNGnGTLX.problem: Existing graph anomaly detectors struggle to identify nodes whose text is plausible in isolation but semantically incompatible with their relational context without anomaly labels.
gCcNGnGTLX.method: CARNet is an unsupervised framework that compares attribute-based and structure-based community distributions to expose semantic conflicts and integrates local and global graph context to infer expected node semantics. For self-supervised training, it creates synthetic contextual mismatches by mixing attributes from semantically dissimilar nodes in different communities while keeping the target's relational context fixed.
gCcNGnGTLX.key_idea: Compares attribute and structural community distributions and trains self-supervisedly on cross-community attribute swaps within preserved relational contexts to detect semantic graph anomalies.
gCcNGnGTLX.evidence: Evaluated via experiments on text-attributed graph anomaly detection benchmarks (specific datasets not stated in abstract).

P6EnVJlhxB.one_liner: Introduces PokeWorld to probe how prediction targets and horizons shape physical parameter identifiability in multimodal latent world models.
P6EnVJlhxB.problem: It is unclear which latent physical parameters action-conditioned world models actually encode, how training targets shape those representations, and whether linear readout reflects predictive use.
P6EnVJlhxB.method: The authors build PokeWorld, a simulated pushing environment where visually identical objects vary in mass, drag, and contact stiffness across episodes. They measure parameter recoverability from raw observations versus matched action-conditioned world models (4M to 56M parameters, RSSMs, and frozen-encoder predictors) while varying prediction targets (e.g., predicting touch vs input-only touch) and horizons.
P6EnVJlhxB.key_idea: Probes physical parameter recoverability and forecast behavior across visually identical objects in PokeWorld while varying prediction targets, horizons, and model architectures.
P6EnVJlhxB.evidence: Controlled experiments in PokeWorld and planar MuJoCo across 4M–56M parameter world models, RSSMs, and frozen encoders with up to 4x data scaling.

xsRcHU2pEk.one_liner: Diagnoses boundary-induced degradation of neural QEC decoders on never-reset syndrome streams and restores performance via interior-window fine-tuning.
xsRcHU2pEk.problem: Neural quantum error correction decoders that beat correlated matching on reset-bounded memory benchmarks fall behind on uninterrupted never-reset syndrome streams.
xsRcHU2pEk.method: Using controlled interventions on surface-code streams at distances d=5, 7, 9, the authors trace this ranking reversal to boundary effects—specifically a terminal detector layer absent in continuous streams—rather than input length. They fine-tune convolutional, graph, and transformer decoders on interior-window labels (and use joint frame-readout supervision for lattice surgery).
xsRcHU2pEk.key_idea: Traces continuous-stream neural QEC decoder failure to terminal boundary layers in reset-bounded training windows and fine-tunes decoders on interior-window labels.
xsRcHU2pEk.evidence: Simulated surface-code stream experiments at d=5, 7, 9 across convolutional, graph, and transformer decoders versus correlated matching, plus lattice surgery evaluations.
xsRcHU2pEk.claimed_gains: Convolutional checkpoints that beat correlated matching by 12–17% on memory benchmarks fall behind by 1.5–1.7x on interior stream decisions; interior-window fine-tuning with one-window lookahead reduces convolutional per-commit error by 40–45% versus matching in simulation.

OFVWcaGfdi.one_liner: Transfers LoRA skills across model families without data or task priors by evolving inputs where teacher outputs diverge with and without the adapter.
OFVWcaGfdi.problem: LoRA adapters fail to transfer in weight space across different base model families, and existing synthetic-data transfer methods require task names, seed examples, labels, or discriminators.
OFVWcaGfdi.method: After measuring that weight-space LoRA transfer works within a shared parameter basis but fails across model families, the authors propose zero-prior skill elicitation. It searches for inputs where a teacher model's generations with and without the LoRA adapter diverge, evolves those probes for coverage, and distills the adapter-equipped teacher's outputs into the target student without task priors or white-box access.
OFVWcaGfdi.key_idea: Elicits and evolves probe inputs maximizing generation divergence between a teacher with and without a LoRA adapter, then distills the adapter-equipped responses into a new model family.
OFVWcaGfdi.evidence: Evaluated with a 397B MoE teacher transferring to three-seed Qwen students (including 9B) on GSM8K, MATH-500, and IFBench under an 8,192-token budget-controlled setting.
OFVWcaGfdi.claimed_gains: Weight-space transfer across families yields TRR <= 0.08; zero-prior elicitation beats untrained Qwen bases by 0.9–5.8 points and adapter-free distillation by 4.8 points at 2.6–3.0x lower target compute, with 9B gaining +11.6 on MATH-500 and +5.7 on IFBench over base.

Bd1yTJg9o3.one_liner: Jointly self-improves action, world, and value heads in one world-action model using return-prediction discrepancy weighting.
Bd1yTJg9o3.problem: Existing robot self-improvement methods update policies using external predictive models without directly improving the predictive capabilities inside the action-generating model.
Bd1yTJg9o3.method: World-ISI iteratively turns robot execution feedback into joint updates of action generation, world prediction, and value estimation within a single world-action model. Its World-Expectation Optimization (WEO) weights successful actions by the gap between observed returns and predicted values, trains world and value heads on failed rollouts, and keeps auxiliary prediction losses on successful samples.
Bd1yTJg9o3.key_idea: Weights successful policy updates by observed-minus-predicted return discrepancies while routing failed executions to dedicated world- and value-prediction objectives within one model.
Bd1yTJg9o3.evidence: Applied to Cosmos Policy and evaluated on 24 manipulation tasks.

KvH9izsHFW.one_liner: Trains a latent-space semantic evaluator on a frozen understanding backbone to align intermediate text-to-image states.
KvH9izsHFW.problem: Unified understanding-generation models can judge finished images, but their understanding component cannot directly evaluate noisy intermediate latent states during long-prompt generation.
KvH9izsHFW.method: Trust-to-Latent attaches a prompt-conditioned latent evidence interface that exposes multi-layer generator features to a reader built on a frozen understanding backbone, trained with image-level preferences transferred across shared-noise latent pairs. Once frozen, this evaluator provides relative preferences over candidate branches from common intermediate states to train the generator with no inference-time reward overhead.
KvH9izsHFW.key_idea: Transfers image-level preferences via shared-noise latent pairs to train a frozen-backbone latent reader that scores intermediate generator branches.
KvH9izsHFW.evidence: Evaluated across five public benchmarks against the base model and reward-optimization baselines.

kTadrHuAgc.one_liner: Augments a frozen DINOv3 representation autoencoder with an opacity signal, detail code, and adapter for RGBA generation.
kTadrHuAgc.problem: A single RGB composite does not uniquely determine foreground color and opacity across backgrounds, preventing direct reuse of pretrained RGB generators for transparent RGBA assets.
kTadrHuAgc.method: AlphaRAE combines frozen DINOv3 features, an opacity signal, and a small learned color-opacity detail code fed into a shared four-channel RGBA decoder. After training and freezing this codec alongside a pretrained RGB diffusion transformer, a learned adapter maps RGB generator outputs into the RGBA decoder input space.
kTadrHuAgc.key_idea: Pairs frozen DINOv3 features with an opacity signal and compact detail code in a shared RGBA decoder, then adapts frozen RGB diffusion outputs post-sampling.
kTadrHuAgc.evidence: Evaluated on 434 test assets at 1024×1024 against AlphaVAE and with a pretrained 256×256 class-conditioned RGB generator against a color-refinement baseline.
kTadrHuAgc.claimed_gains: At 1024×1024 on 434 test assets, the codec reaches 38.83 dB PSNR and 0.01463 LPIPS with 67% lower Alpha L1 than AlphaVAE.

gvhGB5w5GZ.one_liner: Constructs whole-brain functional atlases by decomposing frozen fMRI autoencoder masked reconstructions into redundant, unique, and synergistic contributions.
gvhGB5w5GZ.problem: Conventional functional brain parcellation relies on signal or representational similarity and fails to distinguish how regions share information or jointly predict distant brain activity.
gvhGB5w5GZ.method: BrainSaber introduces Reconstruction-based Information Decomposition (RID), which masks a frozen pretrained fMRI autoencoder to compare target reconstructions from individual versus paired sources and separate redundant, unique, and synergistic predictive contributions. It combines these components with brain-wide predictive flow and spatial constraints to form contiguous cortical and non-cortical parcels.
gvhGB5w5GZ.key_idea: Applies controlled single- and paired-source masking to a frozen pretrained fMRI autoencoder to decompose target reconstruction into redundant, unique, and synergistic components for brain parcellation.
gvhGB5w5GZ.evidence: Evaluated via cortical and whole-brain homogeneity and separability analyses, downstream prediction across five datasets, and cross-window and cross-session repeatability tests.

094XMxiFom.one_liner: Estimates low-rank gradients without bias via fixed-rank sampling without replacement and second-moment subspace alignment for memory-efficient training.
094XMxiFom.problem: Existing low-rank gradient estimators either introduce bias (deterministic top-k) or suffer high variance (randomized estimators), widening the optimization gap to full-rank training.
094XMxiFom.method: PLUMAGE performs fixed-rank sampling without replacement to obtain an unbiased minimum-variance low-rank gradient estimator for a given rank budget, requiring only k extra scale factors per layer. It pairs this with a numerically robust second-moment alignment procedure for alternating subspaces in stateful optimizers and transfers to Muon-style SUMO.
094XMxiFom.key_idea: Uses fixed-rank sampling without replacement for unbiased minimum-variance low-rank gradient estimation paired with second-moment alignment across alternating optimizer subspaces.
094XMxiFom.evidence: Evaluated on pre-training and fine-tuning (including 130M, 350M, and 1B scales) comparing against GALORE, full-rank Adam, and Muon/SUMO.
094XMxiFom.claimed_gains: Reduces the optimization gap to full-rank training by 36% on average over GALORE within ~1% runtime, cuts 1B pre-training steps to GALORE's terminal loss by 30%, and reduces SUMO's perplexity gap to full-rank Muon by ~40% at 130M and 350M scales.

4qddTfOQac.one_liner: Builds a runtime typed provenance graph over multi-agent events to localize harmful state and execute selective recovery actions.
4qddTfOQac.problem: Locally benign messages in multi-agent systems can propagate harm through shared memory or tools, while existing runtime controls only flag risks or halt entire runs without specifying state repair.
4qddTfOQac.method: TRACE-MAS constructs a typed event graph of messages, state transitions, and tool calls at each checkpoint, localizes likely root causes and affected downstream scope, and selects permissible recovery actions through a shared action-permission interface.
4qddTfOQac.key_idea: Maintain a checkpointed typed provenance graph over multi-agent messages, state changes, and tool calls to localize root causes and apply scoped recovery actions.
4qddTfOQac.evidence: Evaluated via paired trajectory replay on TRACE-Bench against a matched Direct-risk control across resource competition, deliberation, shared memory, tool transfer, and bargaining interfaces.
4qddTfOQac.claimed_gains: In the matched resource-competition comparison, TRACE-MAS lowers Harm by 12.0% and ASR by 49.0% while raising Utility by 13.0% relative to Direct-risk.

bKtriz3SuM.one_liner: Evolves executable agent memory programs along individual capability dimensions and consolidates specialists via differential trace integration.
bKtriz3SuM.problem: Holistic self-evolution of agent memory programs optimizes aggregate scores from mixed feedback, obscuring capability-specific improvements masked by regressions elsewhere.
bKtriz3SuM.method: PrisMem selects target capabilities using dependency-aware prioritization, refines capability-specialist memory programs via history-guided diagnosis, and merges complementary gains into one program using trace-guided integration over paired differential cases.
bKtriz3SuM.key_idea: Evolve specialist agent memory programs per capability dimension with dependency-aware selection and consolidate them by comparing behavioral traces on paired differential cases.
bKtriz3SuM.evidence: Evaluated on million-token memory benchmarks BEAM-1M and LongMemEval-M against memory baselines.
bKtriz3SuM.claimed_gains: Outperforms the strongest baselines by 10.54 percentage points on BEAM-1M and 7.83 percentage points on LongMemEval-M.

v4zSwenn2E.one_liner: Trains diverse multi-generator detection experts by marginal loss reduction and calibrates local scores against real-image global-local baselines.
v4zSwenn2E.problem: AI-generated image detectors overfit generator-specific artifacts and misclassify normal local variations in unfamiliar real images as synthetic.
v4zSwenn2E.method: EviCal trains multiple lightweight experts guided by each expert's marginal loss reduction so experts generalize across multiple generators while specializing on different images, then calibrates global and local scores on held-out real images by discounting high local responses consistent with normal real-image global-local relations.
v4zSwenn2E.key_idea: Train multi-expert detectors for cross-generator usefulness and image diversity via marginal loss reduction, then discount local scores consistent with held-out real-image global-local statistics.
v4zSwenn2E.evidence: Trained on four GenImage generators and evaluated cross-generator on Chameleon and AIGI-Now.
v4zSwenn2E.claimed_gains: Trained on four GenImage generators, EviCal achieves 91.46% accuracy on Chameleon and 95.74% average accuracy on AIGI-Now.

8bxrbbOHsv.one_liner: Compresses visual tokens via video-codec frame grouping, merges stationary captions, and grounds decoding in metadata for robot memory.
8bxrbbOHsv.problem: Caption-based spatio-temporal robot memory is too expensive for on-device execution due to redundant visual tokens, repeated captions, and local reasoners declining to transcribe stored quantitative fields.
8bxrbbOHsv.method: CaRAMeL applies three training-free mechanisms: Chimera token compression keeps one intact reference frame per group and encodes only changed regions in a second frame; caption compression merges consecutive captions while odometry stays within a bounded radius without dropping segment poses or timestamps; and evidence-grounded decoding anchors quantitative fields directly in retrieved metadata.
8bxrbbOHsv.key_idea: Groups video frames into reference and changed-region tokens, merges bounded-radius captions while retaining pose-timestamp metadata, and grounds quantitative decoding directly in retrieved metadata fields.
8bxrbbOHsv.evidence: Evaluated on NaVQA with an 8B local reasoner.
8bxrbbOHsv.claimed_gains: Operates on two-thirds of the visual tokens and a 40% smaller memory store on NaVQA.

1roHwQ9Wdi.one_liner: Uses a task-level cluster bootstrap certificate to bound error rates when automating LLM agent trajectory evaluation.
1roHwQ9Wdi.problem: Automatic judges for LLM agent trajectories lack valid error-rate guarantees because trajectories from the same task form correlated clusters that break i.i.d. selective-judging certificates.
1roHwQ9Wdi.method: The authors prove no uniformly valid and useful certificate exists below roughly 29 tasks, introduce a task-level bootstrap certificate that respects task clustering, and pair it with a fine-tuned 4B logprob judge for selective automation.
1roHwQ9Wdi.key_idea: Resamples at the task-cluster level via a bootstrap certificate to calibrate a logprob judge's abstention threshold under correlated agent trajectories.
1roHwQ9Wdi.evidence: Supported by an impossibility proof, adversarial simulations, eleven real judge-corpus pools, and a fine-tuned 4B logprob judge tested on tool-use and web corpora across three seeds.
1roHwQ9Wdi.claimed_gains: The task-level bootstrap certificate meets its confidence level by 32 tasks and stays within it from 50 tasks; a fine-tuned 4B logprob judge certifies 0.34 to 0.61 of evaluation at alpha=0.1 (30-59% automation in TL;DR), whereas a naive i.i.d. certificate claims 98% automation while exceeding the error budget in 17.5% of task resamples.

4TxphVYPCA.one_liner: Routes each query to token-level KV states or learned multi-scale segment summaries via a hierarchical sparse attention operator.
4TxphVYPCA.problem: Long-context LLM inference is bottlenecked by the memory-bandwidth cost of reading an ever-growing key-value cache during attention.
4TxphVYPCA.method: Hierarchical Adaptive Sparse Attention (HASA) organizes each layer's KV cache into token-level entries and learned summaries over progressively larger segments, with a per-query, per-layer learned router selecting the resolution for each historical span. The summaries and router are trained via distillation and task-level fine-tuning while keeping the LLM backbone frozen, paired with a fused decode kernel.
4TxphVYPCA.key_idea: Maintains a multi-resolution hierarchy of token-level KV states and learned segment summaries, using a per-query router to select each span's attention resolution.
4TxphVYPCA.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3-8B across all sixteen English LongBench tasks and decode latency benchmarks at 65K and 131K context lengths against full attention and FlashAttention-3.
4TxphVYPCA.claimed_gains: Improves Qwen3-8B average score across sixteen English LongBench tasks by +1.1 points over full attention while attending to 4.3x fewer KV entries, and reduces decode latency over FlashAttention-3 by 17.2% at 65K and 25.8% at 131K.

kZJGzT3BR2.one_liner: Contextualizes egocentric video-audio memories into multi-view indices and performs question-conditioned temporal retrieval.
kZJGzT3BR2.problem: Existing egocentric memory pipelines store isolated video captions or transcripts and query them directly, losing situational context, cross-modal links, and implicit temporal intent.
kZJGzT3BR2.method: EgoCITE uses EgoScheme to convert fragmentary captions and transcripts into self-contained atomic memories using local multimodal context, EgoIndex to build multi-view, multi-granularity indices over actions, activities, utterances, and conversations, and EgoRetrv to score question-conditioned temporal relevance and iteratively retrieve and curate evidence.
kZJGzT3BR2.key_idea: Rewrites fragments into context-complete atomic memories, indexes them across multi-view action-activity-utterance-conversation granularities, and scores temporal relevance conditioned on the question.
kZJGzT3BR2.evidence: Evaluated on EgoLifeQA, EgoMem, and EgoR1-Bench measuring answer accuracy and target-event retrieval alignment against agentic memory baselines.

Zf68SX9abN.one_liner: Runs autoregressive video diffusion at high noise levels before switching to bidirectional parallel diffusion at low noise.
Zf68SX9abN.problem: Bidirectional video diffusion models denoise entire videos in parallel and still violate physical laws and symbolic rules even when trained on unlimited procedural data, whereas fully autoregressive diffusion is slow.
Zf68SX9abN.method: Serial-to-Parallel Diffusion (S2PD) performs autoregressive serial denoising at high noise levels to compute valid state transitions and then transitions to bidirectional parallel denoising at low noise to jointly refine the full video. It is implemented both in a from-scratch pixel-space diffusion transformer and by LoRA fine-tuning a pretrained video model.
Zf68SX9abN.key_idea: Splits video denoising into an autoregressive high-noise stage for valid state transitions followed by a bidirectional low-noise stage for joint refinement.
Zf68SX9abN.evidence: Evaluated with a from-scratch pixel-space diffusion transformer and a LoRA-adapted pretrained video model across games, physical simulations, and real video against bidirectional and serial baselines.

dmWiArTSoB.one_liner: Filters uncurated 3D reconstruction image sets by repeatedly validating views against scene-consistent anchors in bounded subsets.
dmWiArTSoB.problem: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction degrades on uncurated image collections containing distractors and geometrically incompatible views, while joint all-image filtering exceeds memory budgets and single-window filtering drops valid views.
dmWiArTSoB.method: Multi-Anchor Context Validation (MACV) is a training-free front-end that samples memory-feasible subsets of the image collection, validates each image against small sets of scene-consistent anchors across subsets, and retains any image supported by at least one anchor in any subset.
dmWiArTSoB.key_idea: Repeatedly validates candidate views against scene-consistent anchor sets within bounded memory-feasible subsets and retains views supported in any subset.
dmWiArTSoB.evidence: Evaluated across multiple datasets and feed-forward 3D reconstruction backbones on view filtering quality and downstream camera pose, depth, and point-cloud metrics.

w8aZY88Jbh.one_liner: Introduces ReVA, a scene-centric UAV video question-answering benchmark built via semi-automatic LLM/MLLM annotation and human verification.
w8aZY88Jbh.problem: Existing remote sensing multimodal benchmarks rely on repetitive template-driven questions and static images, failing to evaluate spatiotemporal reasoning over UAV videos.
w8aZY88Jbh.method: The authors build ReVA, containing 2,438 drone videos across 18 cities (580K frames) and 22K question-answer pairs spanning 11 QA tasks, generated through a semi-automatic Text LLM and MLLM pipeline with human verification.
w8aZY88Jbh.key_idea: Constructs a scene-centric UAV video QA benchmark via semi-automatic LLM and MLLM question generation paired with human verification across 11 spatiotemporal tasks.
w8aZY88Jbh.evidence: Evaluates 23 proprietary and open-source Video LLMs on ReVA's 2,438 drone videos and 22K QA pairs.

wSHvuy1308.one_liner: Pretrains tabular foundation models on synthetic fairness tasks with a gradient reversal layer for single-pass fair predictions.
wSHvuy1308.problem: Tabular foundation models lack fairness guarantees in high-stakes tasks because sensitive attributes are scarce in training data and existing fairness methods do not fit in-context learning.
wSHvuy1308.method: FairTFM pretrains a tabular foundation model on synthetic fairness tasks using a fairness-aware architecture equipped with a gradient reversal layer so learned representations remain invariant to sensitive attributes in a single forward pass without task-specific retraining.
wSHvuy1308.key_idea: Combines synthetic fairness pretraining tasks with a gradient reversal layer to enforce sensitive-attribute-invariant representations during tabular in-context learning.
wSHvuy1308.evidence: Evaluated on 120 fairness tasks measuring fairness improvements and predictive accuracy.

0FBmlQimVO.one_liner: Conditions World-Action Models on imagined 4D world-frame pointmaps, scene flow, and wrist-view depth alongside RGB futures.
0FBmlQimVO.problem: World-Action Models that imagine only RGB futures entangle physical geometry and motion with texture, illumination, and camera movement, limiting control robustness.
0FBmlQimVO.method: The authors represent observable 4D state using world-frame pointmaps, scene flow, and wrist-view depth, explicitly imagine future 4D geometry alongside RGB futures, feed both directly into action generation, and select geometric supervision by view-specific reliability.
0FBmlQimVO.key_idea: Explicitly predicts future world-frame pointmaps, scene flow, and wrist depth alongside RGB and exposes these geometric futures directly to the action policy.
0FBmlQimVO.evidence: Controlled studies on LIBERO-Plus Long comparing a matched LingBot-VA baseline and alternative geometric interfaces under sensor noise, lighting, and background shifts.
0FBmlQimVO.claimed_gains: Improves a matched LingBot-VA baseline from 73.73% to 82.73% on LIBERO-Plus Long.

sBvEgtiF5l.one_liner: Contrasts crop-conditioned teacher distributions across verified semantically replaced image pairs during visual on-policy distillation.
sBvEgtiF5l.problem: Standard visual on-policy distillation on individual images does not isolate how target visual details versus surrounding context drive teacher answer preferences.
sBvEgtiF5l.method: CF-OPD constructs verified counterfactual image pairs via semantic replacement with different correct answers; at each student-generated prefix, it contrasts the two crop-conditioned teacher distributions to adjust a student-anchored distribution before mixing with the current crop teacher across independent rollouts. The authors also introduce CF-Bench-X (595 verified semantic pairs) with Flip and Blind rate metrics.
sBvEgtiF5l.key_idea: Uses the contrast between crop-conditioned teacher distributions on semantically replaced image pairs to adjust student-anchored on-policy distillation targets at each prefix.
sBvEgtiF5l.evidence: Evaluated on six visual benchmarks and CF-Bench-X (595 pairs) across Qwen3.5-based methods at two scales including 9B.

L0Kgn7Uyx4.one_liner: Adapts tabular foundation models with differential privacy via gradient-based learnable context tuning (TabDPSGD) or output-only teacher aggregation (TabPATE).
L0Kgn7Uyx4.problem: Providing sensitive labeled records as in-context examples to tabular foundation models exposes training records to membership inference attacks.
L0Kgn7Uyx4.method: After instantiating membership inference attacks against tabular ICL, the authors propose TabDPSGD, which privately trains a learnable context and a parameter subset with DP-SGD, and TabPATE, which partitions private data across TFM teachers and privately aggregates predictions on synthetic queries to build a student ICL context using only model outputs.
L0Kgn7Uyx4.key_idea: Protects private tabular ICL data either by DP-SGD tuning of a learnable context and weights or by PATE-style private ensemble labeling of synthetic context queries.
L0Kgn7Uyx4.evidence: Membership inference attack demonstrations and private adaptation experiments across seven datasets and two tabular foundation models against private baselines.
L0Kgn7Uyx4.claimed_gains: TabDPSGD beats the strongest evaluated private baseline on six of seven datasets.

26oXJe49qk.one_liner: Introduces MemGym, a six-track benchmark isolating agent memory modules from reasoning, plus a 1.7B local compression scorer.
26oXJe49qk.problem: Chat memory benchmarks miss agentic context-management decisions, while end-task agent benchmarks conflate memory failures with reasoning and tool-use errors.
26oXJe49qk.method: MemGym inserts a swappable memory module between interaction history and a fixed reasoner across six tracks (including four wrapped agent benchmarks plus controlled-context MemGym-CodeQA and MemGym-DR with recoverability checks), and trains a 1.7B-parameter MemRM scorer to predict whether post-compression next actions reproduce reference outputs on SWE-Gym.
26oXJe49qk.key_idea: Decouples agent memory from fixed environments and reasoners across six tracks, pairing recoverability-checked tasks with a 1.7B local action-preservation scorer.
26oXJe49qk.evidence: Evaluates eight memory strategies across four reasoning models on six tracks including SWE-Gym, MemGym-CodeQA, and MemGym-DR.

rqKuKaFBIK.one_liner: Introduces MeshSplatBench to evaluate triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering under graphics-engine deployment protocols and topological audits.
rqKuKaFBIK.problem: Triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering methods are evaluated under inconsistent settings and rarely tested for actual deployment inside standard graphics engines.
rqKuKaFBIK.method: MeshSplatBench provides a unified evaluation covering Non-Engine Render evaluation, Standard deployment (opaque mesh with vertex colors and hardware Z-buffering), Dedicated deployment (engine implementations supporting features like alpha blending), and a structural topological audit of exported surfaces.
rqKuKaFBIK.key_idea: Standardizes triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering evaluation with dual graphics-engine deployment protocols (Standard and Dedicated) and exported-surface topological auditing.
rqKuKaFBIK.evidence: Defines and applies the MeshSplatBench evaluation protocol and structural audit across triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering methods.

AofsFkzJyv.one_liner: Groups co-acting multi-agent outputs into dynamic active sets with shared advantages, combined clipping, and set-size normalization.
AofsFkzJyv.problem: Updating individual agent responses independently splits coupled decisions, while treating entire trajectories as single updates conflates decisions made under different observations.
AofsFkzJyv.method: Setwise Relative Policy Optimization (SRPO) groups outputs jointly responsible for a single state transition into an active set (singleton for division of labor, multi-element for co-evolution), assigns a shared advantage to each active set, clips the combined policy update, and normalizes its scale by set size.
AofsFkzJyv.key_idea: Defines RL policy updates at the active-set level for each state transition using shared advantages, joint policy clipping, and set-size normalization.
AofsFkzJyv.evidence: Experiments are mentioned in the abstract, though specific datasets, models, and metrics are not stated in the available text.

JwUvLVBgt7.one_liner: Tests whether VLM reasoning steps rely on cited bounding boxes by comparing step log-likelihood drops under own- vs other-region perturbations.
JwUvLVBgt7.problem: Localization metrics only check whether VLM-cited bounding boxes match ground-truth regions, not whether each reasoning step actually depends on the region it cites.
