JwUvLVBgt7.method: The authors propose an annotation-free step-specific intervention test that perturbs each cited region in turn, measures every fixed step's mean per-token log-likelihood change, and computes the bidirectional own-region ordering probability against regions cited by other steps in the same chain (bounded at <=50% under an additive null model).
JwUvLVBgt7.key_idea: Compares each reasoning step's log-likelihood sensitivity to perturbing its own cited box versus boxes cited by other steps, testing against a 50% exchangeable null.
JwUvLVBgt7.evidence: Theoretical null bound plus experiments on Qwen3-VL-4B across three image-disjoint GQA cohorts and A-OKVQA, including preregistered context/perturbation variations and step regeneration.
JwUvLVBgt7.claimed_gains: Qwen3-VL-4B achieves ~61% own-region ordering probability across three GQA cohorts and 72% on A-OKVQA, remaining above 50% (lowest point estimate 58%) across all preregistered scoring-context and intervention-operator changes.

OAX2QPoTJg.one_liner: Routes visual queries through global linear attention and text tokens through sliding-window attention while keeping 25% full-attention layers.
OAX2QPoTJg.problem: Quadratic softmax attention bottlenecks long-context VLMs and video generation, while uniform attention hybrids ignore modality differences between diffuse visual attention and local text retrieval.
OAX2QPoTJg.method: HyLin introduces Hybrid Linear-coupled Window Attention (HLWA), which routes visual queries through a constant-state global linear attention stream and applies sliding-window attention to text queries, keys, and values before restoring multimodal order. Theory-guided calibration retains 25% of high-risk layers as full attention, trained via a four-stage alignment, selection, distillation, and supervised curriculum.
OAX2QPoTJg.key_idea: Splits multimodal attention by modality—global linear attention for visual queries and sliding-window attention for text—while retaining 25% calibrated full-attention layers.
OAX2QPoTJg.evidence: Teacher-attention heterogeneity analysis across modalities, heads, and depth, plus calibration and training for VLM and video DiT architectures.

pK04w5wiDp.one_liner: Interleaves evidence acquisition, typed claim-evidence graph updates, and label-free verifier auditing for test-time scaling.
pK04w5wiDp.problem: Test-time scaling typically treats verification as a terminal scoring step detached from evidence gathering, provenance tracking, and auditing unreliable verifiers.
pK04w5wiDp.method: GEVA runs a deterministic state-action-observation loop over a typed claim-evidence graph, combining execution probes, knowledge-base traversals, and model adjudication under contracts tracking dependence, supersession, disclosure, and repair, alongside premise-qualified wrongness certificates that audit external evidence producers without labels.
pK04w5wiDp.key_idea: Maintains a typed claim-evidence provenance graph in a closed state-action-observation verification loop with label-free wrongness certificates for auditing evidence producers.
pK04w5wiDp.evidence: Evaluated across seven regimes spanning code, text-to-SQL, knowledge-graph QA (MetaQA-3hop, KQA Pro), and multiple-choice reasoning, with matched-evidence controls and a disjoint held-out audit split.
pK04w5wiDp.claimed_gains: Reaches 42.70% on MetaQA-3hop (+11.10 points over Fixed V) and 61.90% on KQA Pro (+5.50 points over Fixed V), reduces closed-loop single-GPU latency by 32.3%-48.5% over iterative tool-feedback loops, and restores 4.38 accuracy points on a held-out split by withdrawing a harmful judge.

wcae0JKDe0.one_liner: Trains a few-step latent motion generator with per-step learned geometric feedback correcting latent velocity from estimated joint geometry.
wcae0JKDe0.problem: Controllable human motion generation faces a trade-off between expensive test-time optimization for accurate joint control and large joint errors in fast few-step generators.
wcae0JKDe0.method: MoGeFi trains a one- and few-step conditional latent motion backbone directly without a diffusion teacher, and adds proposal-based geometric feedback that estimates joint geometry from the current state at each step to correct latent velocity via geometric and distributional supervision on short rollouts.
wcae0JKDe0.key_idea: Refreshes estimated joint geometry at each few-step sampling iteration to drive learned forward-only velocity corrections trained on short model rollouts.
wcae0JKDe0.evidence: Evaluated with ablations on HumanML3D across multiple motion generation tasks including sparse joint control against MaskControl-Fast.
wcae0JKDe0.claimed_gains: Achieves comparable FID while roughly halving trajectory and location error rates compared with MaskControl-Fast, generating each sequence in approximately 61 ms.

uDIdkCH4DV.one_liner: Instantiates recording-specific continuous EEG neural fields from unordered electrode supports via temporal-spectral conditioning and dual-support training.
uDIdkCH4DV.problem: EEG spatial super-resolution must reconstruct missing or unseen electrodes across varying sensor layouts while adapting to each recording's temporal and spectral characteristics.
uDIdkCH4DV.method: ScalpINR is an amortized support-conditioned neural field that maps an unordered set of observed EEG signals and coordinates to recording-dependent temporal and spectral controls for a shared coordinate decoder, trained with a dual-support objective to align fields inferred from different electrode subsets without test-time optimization.
uDIdkCH4DV.key_idea: Generates recording-specific temporal and spectral decoder controls from unordered observed electrodes and trains with a dual-support consistency loss across electrode subsets.
uDIdkCH4DV.evidence: Evaluated on SEED, EEG-AAD, and BCI2000 under random missing-channel reconstruction and strict held-out-electrode evaluation.
uDIdkCH4DV.claimed_gains: Reduces NMSE by 22.4% relative to the strongest baseline on EEG-AAD when all non-held-out electrodes are available as support.

hNkuYHn7Ty.one_liner: Zeroes a sparse pre-selected set of hidden-state coordinates at the final prefill token of one VLM layer to complement activation steering.
hNkuYHn7Ty.problem: Increasing activation steering strength to fix residual VLM jailbreak failures degrades benign utility.
hNkuYHn7Ty.method: SCOPE identifies a sparse set of hidden-state coordinates with large pre-generation magnitude differences between safe- and unsafe-response prompts on an unmodified base VLM, then zeroes those coordinates at one language decoder layer at the final prompt position during prefill across steering methods and attacks.
hNkuYHn7Ty.key_idea: Selects response-conditioned sparse hidden-state coordinates once on a base VLM and zeroes them at the final prompt token during prefill.
hNkuYHn7Ty.evidence: Evaluated across 18 combinations of two VLMs, three steering methods, and three jailbreak benchmarks (fixed and transfer attacks), plus matched-intervention support and operator ablations.
hNkuYHn7Ty.claimed_gains: Reduces attack success rates by 1.78 to 14.80 percentage points across all 18 evaluated combinations while largely preserving benign utility.

V7gMQjOqcP.one_liner: Expands extra rollouts from isolated task snapshots and anchors self-rewards to single live user feedback during agent deployment.
V7gMQjOqcP.problem: Training self-hosted LLM agents from sequential deployment tasks with only single-feedback evaluation per task suffers from an exploration bottleneck under single-rollout RL.
V7gMQjOqcP.method: The authors introduce DEAL, an executable deployment-learning testbed for workplace assistance and AI research, and propose Self-Rewarded Exploration (SRE), which branches additional trajectories from isolated task snapshots and uses the single live user feedback as an anchor to assign self-rewards.
V7gMQjOqcP.key_idea: Expands multiple trajectories from isolated task snapshots and assigns self-rewards anchored to the single live deployment feedback.
V7gMQjOqcP.evidence: Supported by a theoretical trade-off analysis of rollout expansion versus self-reward error and experiments on DEAL with Gemma4-E4B-IT and Qwen3.5-9B.

moFf9vJeAN.one_liner: Routes each token to hardware-aligned attention-head and FFN-channel groups with reordered masks for GPU block-skipping kernels.
moFf9vJeAN.problem: Static structured pruning hurts LLM quality at high sparsity, whereas fine-grained dynamic pruning causes irregular execution that erases hardware speedups.
moFf9vJeAN.method: WIDE uses end-to-end differentiable routers to select GQA-aligned query-head groups and GPU-tile-aligned FFN-channel groups per token, then reorders routing masks to cluster active tokens within each group so co-designed GPU kernels can skip inactive loads and tensor-core operations during both prefill and decoding.
moFf9vJeAN.key_idea: Selects GQA-aligned head groups and tile-aligned FFN channels per token via differentiable routers and reorders masks to cluster active tokens for block-skipping kernels.
moFf9vJeAN.evidence: Evaluated on the Llama3 (including Llama3.1-8B) and Qwen3 families against static and dynamic pruning baselines under calibration-only settings.
moFf9vJeAN.claimed_gains: At 50% target routing sparsity, improves Llama3.1-8B average zero-shot accuracy by up to 20.26 points over the strongest dynamic-depth baseline under calibration-only settings, retaining 97.6%/88.2% of dense performance.

wm97mtaTWL.one_liner: Introduces the SolveEdit visual problem-solving benchmark with atomic transition contracts and a two-stage visual planner.
wm97mtaTWL.problem: Existing image-editing benchmarks test perception, generation, or explicit edit instructions rather than inferring and executing goal-driven scene transformations while preserving unrelated content.
wm97mtaTWL.method: SolveEdit comprises 2,728 cases across 10 domains and 54 subdomains scored by SolveScore using atomic transition contracts specifying required and protected conditions without a single reference image; SolveEditPlan adds a two-stage visual planner that instantiates the transition before image generation.
wm97mtaTWL.key_idea: Evaluates goal-driven visual edits via atomic required/protected transition contracts without single reference outputs, and plans transitions in two stages before generation.
wm97mtaTWL.evidence: Benchmarks generators on SolveEdit's 2,728 cases and evaluates SolveEditPlan under matched single-generation settings across three image generators.
wm97mtaTWL.claimed_gains: The strongest evaluated model reaches 57.0% SolveScore; SolveEditPlan improves SolveScore by 9.1 points on average across three generators, including from 57.0% to 71.6% on one generator.

vSjw3bWmyF.one_liner: Computes closed-form quadratic Shapley expert attributions and mass-conserving counterfactual router swaps for sparse MoE models.
vSjw3bWmyF.problem: Routing frequency and gate weights measure MoE expert usage rather than how co-routed experts jointly contribute to loss or how useful router choices are.
vSjw3bWmyF.method: CONTRAIL models co-routed experts as a cooperative game to derive closed-form Shapley values from a quadratic loss approximation in a single backward pass, and evaluates router decisions via a Coalition-Consistent Gate Estimator that performs a mass-conserving counterfactual swap between the nearest selected and excluded experts.
vSjw3bWmyF.key_idea: Derives single-backward-pass quadratic Shapley values for co-routed experts and estimates router utility via mass-conserving counterfactual swaps with the nearest excluded expert.
vSjw3bWmyF.evidence: Evaluated on four instruction-tuned sparse MoE models across WikiText-2, GSM8K, MMLU, and MedQA for expert removal, cross-task intervention, router analysis, and sparse fine-tuning.

D0cLnmHjUF.one_liner: Abstracts agent interaction trajectories progressively into episodic descriptions, reusable procedures, and guiding principles for continual evolution.
D0cLnmHjUF.problem: External agent memory systems keep stored experiences tightly coupled to specific tasks and contexts, limiting cross-task generalization without parameter fine-tuning.
D0cLnmHjUF.method: SAGA (Self-evolving Agents through Experience-Grounded Abstraction) builds an external memory framework that progressively abstracts raw interaction trajectories into episodic descriptions, reusable procedures, and general principles to guide future agent actions.
D0cLnmHjUF.key_idea: Progressively distills concrete agent trajectories into hierarchical episodic descriptions, reusable procedures, and abstract principles in external memory.

RIpEtbedmF.one_liner: Repairs frozen latent world model planning using latent path local targets, goal-conditioned action-chunk priors, and min-over-horizon costs.
RIpEtbedmF.problem: Long-horizon visual control with latent world models fails due to mismatches between distant goals and short rollouts, uninformed action search, and restrictive terminal-only rollout costs.
RIpEtbedmF.method: LeWM++ wraps a frozen latent world model with three components: LatentPathFlow generates a temporally aligned latent path whose endpoint serves as a local target, a final-goal-conditioned Action Chunk Prior guides CEM search with coherent action chunks, and Min-over-Horizon scores each rollout by its closest approach to the local target.
RIpEtbedmF.key_idea: Combines latent-path local targets, final-goal-conditioned action-chunk proposals for CEM, and min-over-horizon rollout scoring around a frozen latent world model.
RIpEtbedmF.evidence: Evaluated on the LeWM Control Suite across four goal offsets and across eight visual OGBench datasets.
RIpEtbedmF.claimed_gains: Lead over LeWM on the LeWM Control Suite grows from 12.0 to 32.3 percentage points as goal distance increases, and LeWM++ achieves 50.62% average score across eight visual OGBench datasets.

6N8dYXmsNk.one_liner: Trains VLMs on corrupted inputs using their own clean-input predictions as token-level on-policy self-distillation targets.
6N8dYXmsNk.problem: VLM post-training typically depends on human annotations, external teacher models, RLHF, or verifiable answers, limiting self-improvement without external supervision.
6N8dYXmsNk.method: NOPD (Noisy Student On-Policy Self-Distillation) feeds corrupted inputs to a VLM and trains it with token-level supervision generated by the same model on the corresponding clean inputs, requiring no external teacher or ground-truth labels.
6N8dYXmsNk.key_idea: Uses the prediction gap between clean and corrupted inputs to provide token-level on-policy self-distillation supervision from the model itself.
6N8dYXmsNk.evidence: Evaluated on five visual reasoning tasks, Geometry3K (2.1K samples), MathVista, and 12 benchmarks across three VLM models including Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
6N8dYXmsNk.claimed_gains: Trained with 2.1K Geometry3K samples, NOPD improves Qwen2.5-VL-7B by 20 points on the Geometry3K validation set and yields 7.4 point gains on MathVista.

AnxK3Tb5VS.one_liner: Poisons ~4% of training data with a benign text trigger to force or suppress large-model consultations in collaborative agents.
AnxK3Tb5VS.problem: Small-large collaborative LLM agents rely on a learned consultation policy that creates an unexplored backdoor attack surface for inflating cost or degrading accuracy.
AnxK3Tb5VS.method: CONFUNDO poisons training data with a benign natural-language instruction trigger to manipulate the small model's consultation policy in two modes: Denial-of-Wallet (DoW) forces unnecessary large-model calls, while Denial-of-Expert (DoE) suppresses needed calls.
AnxK3Tb5VS.key_idea: Backdoors the small agent's learned consultation router via a benign text trigger to either force 100% escalation (DoW) or suppress escalation to 0% (DoE).
AnxK3Tb5VS.evidence: Evaluated with ~4% poisoned training data on GSM8K and security-sensitive coding tasks, compared against prompt-injection and jailbreak attacks.
AnxK3Tb5VS.claimed_gains: With ~4% poisoned data, DoW reaches 100% consultation rate on triggered inputs in most settings, while DoE drops triggered consultation rate to 0%, reducing GSM8K accuracy from 0.800 to 0.595 and increasing insecure-code generation from 0.356 to 0.488.

5iMbperkQz.one_liner: Evaluates student actions across multiple teacher checkpoints and contexts to extract cross-context consistent on-policy distillation signals.
5iMbperkQz.problem: Single-context on-policy distillation conflates stable learning signals with context-specific teacher preferences.
5iMbperkQz.method: Factorial On-Policy Distillation (FOPD) evaluates identical student actions across teacher checkpoints and task-relevant contexts, centers teacher signals over the student's action distribution, keeps directions consistently supported across contexts with a conservative shared magnitude, and anchors updates to the standard OPD direction.
5iMbperkQz.key_idea: Aggregates centered teacher signals across checkpoints and contexts, retaining only cross-context consistent directions with conservative magnitude anchored to standard OPD.
5iMbperkQz.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3-1.7B (non-thinking mode) across 14 math, code, and science benchmarks with component ablations, matched sparsity/magnitude controls, and token-level analysis.
5iMbperkQz.claimed_gains: Achieves a 43.35 Macro score on Qwen3-1.7B (+5.9% relative gain over the strongest baseline, improving 13 of 14 tasks); ablations drop Macro score by 1.82-5.85 points and matched controls trail by 2.35-2.65 points.

zJgrrCGzU1.one_liner: Uses a training-only auxiliary ANN to cancel shared common-mode Q-value errors in low-timestep deep spiking Q-networks.
zJgrrCGzU1.problem: Reducing simulation timesteps in deep spiking Q-networks severely degrades RL performance because common-mode Q-value errors shared across actions corrupt bootstrapped temporal-difference targets.
zJgrrCGzU1.method: After decomposing Q-value errors into common-mode and differential-mode components, the authors propose CMC-DSQN, which pairs the SNN with an auxiliary ANN during training to compensate for common-mode errors in SNN outputs, then discards the ANN at inference for greedy SNN action selection.
zJgrrCGzU1.key_idea: Trains an auxiliary ANN to offset shared common-mode Q-value errors during TD bootstrapping and removes it at inference so greedy control uses only the SNN.
zJgrrCGzU1.evidence: Error decomposition analysis and experiments on Atari and MiniAtar environments under low-timestep settings.
